title: Being gentle with people, animals and plants
keyIdea: Being gentle means soft hands and kind words. Stroke a pet slowly and softly, and stop when its body says no: flat ears, a swishing tail or walking away. Minibeasts are small and soft, so carry them back to where they live. Plants are alive too: give them water and light, and leave the flowers to grow. With friends, say please, thank you, are you OK and sorry.

kid: Gentle means soft and slow. Soft hands. Kind words.
Stroke a cat or dog slowly, along its back. If it puts its ears flat or walks away, stop. It is saying no more.
A worm, a snail and a ladybird are small and soft. Do not squash them. Put them back where they live.
Plants are alive. Give them a drink of water. Leave the flowers on. With friends, say please and thank you, and ask: are you OK?
adult: At three and four, children are learning to manage their own hands and to notice how others feel. The EYFS framework covers this in Personal, Social and Emotional Development (building relationships, managing self) and in Understanding the World, where children learn to care for and respect living things, from pets and minibeasts to plants. Development Matters lists showing care for living things as part of this age range.

Gentle touch is best taught by showing: take your child's hand and stroke the pet slowly with a flat palm, from head to tail. Name what the animal's body says. A purr or leaning in means yes; flat ears, a swishing tail, a growl or walking away mean stop. Teaching children to stop when an animal moves away also protects them from bites and scratches.

Common mistakes: patting hard and fast because the child is excited; following or picking up a pet that has walked off; keeping a minibeast in a jar or pocket to play with; picking flowers or pulling leaves; and grabbing toys instead of asking. Praise the gentle choice straight away, because young children learn more from praise than from telling off.

In the lab your child strokes a cat slowly (a fast swipe makes it run), reads three cat moods, carries a worm, snail and ladybird home, chooses kind things for a plant, and picks kind words in four friend moments.

familyTip: Practise 'gentle hands' on a soft toy first: slow strokes, head to tail. Then, with a calm pet, stop together when it walks away and say 'it's saying no more'.

practice.prompt: How do we stroke a cat?
practice.hint: Think of soft hands. What does a cat like?
practice.explain: Slowly and softly, along its back. Fast, hard pats can hurt and make the cat run.

practice.prompt: You see {n} snails on the path. What is kind?
choices: Put them back on the leaves
practice.hint: Where do snails live? Look under the leaves.
practice.explain: Put the {n} snails back on the leaves, where they live. A jar is not their home.

practice.prompt: The dog walks away from you. What do you do?
practice.hint: What is the dog's body saying when it walks away?
practice.explain: Let it go. Walking away means no more. It can come back when it wants to.

practice.prompt: Your friend gives you {n} stickers. What do you say?
practice.hint: What do we say when someone is kind to us?
practice.explain: Thank you! Your friend shared {n} stickers, so we say thank you.

pool.prompt: The cat purrs and leans on your hand. What does it mean?
pool.hint: Purring and leaning in is a happy sign.
pool.explain: It likes it. You can keep stroking slowly and softly.

pool.prompt: The cat puts its ears flat. What do you do?
pool.hint: Flat ears are a sign. Is it a yes or a no?
pool.explain: Stop. Flat ears mean the cat has had enough.

pool.prompt: You find {n} worms on the path. What is kind?
pool.hint: Where do worms live? Think of the garden.
pool.explain: Put the {n} worms back on the soil. That is where worms live.

pool.prompt: How can you help a plant?
pool.hint: Plants are alive. What do they need?
pool.explain: Give it some water. Plants need water and light to grow.

pool.prompt: Your friend has the bike. You want a go. What do you say?
choices: Can I have a turn, please?
pool.explain: Can I have a turn, please? Grabbing and pushing can hurt your friend.

pool.prompt: You bump into {n} children by mistake. What do you say?
pool.hint: What do we say when we hurt someone by mistake?
pool.explain: Sorry! Are you OK? Even by mistake, we stop and check the {n} children are all right.

pool.prompt: A ladybird lands on your hand. What do you do?
choices: Let it walk off onto a leaf
pool.explain: Let it walk off onto a leaf. Be still and gentle, so it is not hurt.
